description: Sandbox release-candidate validation coverage register (tempdoc 728, Part B/C). Projection-not-fork applied to release validation: what a clean-Sandbox round must verify DERIVES from what the app ships, instead of being remembered. scripts/sandbox/gen_coverage_brief.py reads the committed surface artifacts (route-manifest cohorts, CorePlugin.ts surface ids, coreInteractionShapes.ts) and FAILS CLOSED if any derived cohort/surface/shape is neither covered nor exempted here — so a newly-shipped surface (the /mcp and trust-panel misses that motivated this doc) can no longer be silently forgotten. Tiers: 'sandbox' = the clean-install / real-GUI / real-external-agent view only the Sandbox has; 'host' = protocol/contract correctness a host test already owns (the Sandbox still confirms reachability); 'sandbox-must-watch' = findings that cannot be CI-gated (Windows trust prompts) and are re-injected into every round's brief (Part C). Same positive-coverage shape as check-ui-step-coverage / check-declared-surfaces.

cohortCoverage.validateHow: On a clean install, confirm an EXTERNAL MCP client reaches POST /mcp: `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector --cli http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp --transport http --method tools/list` returns the tool set. requiredRoutes pins POST /mcp so a token-only GET can't satisfy coverage. Protocol conformance is host-owned (McpProtocolHandlerTest); the Sandbox proves clean-install reachability + discoverability. REQUIRED PROCEDURE for the published TYPED_CONFIRM trust-gate claim (see claims[] below): the Inspector CLI's `--tool-arg` string-coerces every value and CANNOT express `justsearch_ingest`'s `paths: string[]` argument -- do not attempt tools/call through it, that procedure is unfollowable (verified against a real round; see tmp/sandbox evidence from the round that hit this). Instead run the staged driver `node <mapped folder>\mcp-client\mcp-typed-confirm.mjs --target <path>` (see `<mapped folder>\mcp-client\README.md`), which spawns the REAL shipped MCPB stdio bridge (`mcp-client\index.js`, a verbatim copy of packaging/mcpb/server/index.js) as a child process and drives `initialize` -> `notifications/initialized` -> `tools/call justsearch_ingest(paths:[<path>])` over its stdin/stdout -- the same transport a real MCP host (e.g. Claude Desktop) uses, so this exercises the actual shipped artifact. Confirm the tools/call response reports a PENDING authorization (isError:true, 'requires your approval (gate: TYPED_CONFIRM)'), not a silent/immediate ingest. The gate response text does NOT carry the pending id -- mcp-typed-confirm.mjs resolves it itself (via GET /api/advisory/authorization-pending/stream) and prints it as `PENDING_ID=<id>` right after the gate result; read that line, do not hand-scrape SSE. Resolve it via `POST /api/authorizations/approve` with JSON body `{"pendingId": "<id>", "execute": true}` (API-reachable, no GUI needed) -- the body key for the id is `pendingId` (AuthorizationController.handleApprove reads body.pendingId; any other key name for the id 400s), and `execute: true` is MANDATORY: without it the call only mints a consent capsule and returns, it does not dispatch the ingest, because an MCP-originated pending has no live browser caller left to replay the capsule against (see AuthorizationController's handleApprove Javadoc, tempdoc 655 addendum). A prior round's procedure named a different (wrong) body key for the id with no execute flag at all, got 400s, and misfiled the result as "approve never executes the operation" -- a false HIGH regression against this documentation defect, not the product. scripts/ci/check-sandbox-authorization-field.mjs now fails the build if that retired key name reappears here or in mcp-client-README.md. Then confirm the ingest actually proceeds after approval. `tools/list` reachability alone does NOT exercise this claim -- it is a separate, mandatory step this round must perform. STATUS (2026-07-15): a prior PowerShell driver was found to HANG waiting on the tools/call response and has been removed. Live isolation against a running dev stack independently verified: the server is fixed and conformant (notifications/initialized returns 202 Accepted with no body; unknown requests still return -32601), and the shipped bridge driven over stdio by this exact Node driver's message sequence WORKS end-to-end -- initialize succeeds, and tools/call justsearch_ingest with a real array paths returns the TYPED_CONFIRM gate response. The server, the shipped bridge, and this driver's message sequence are live-verified; the round running this procedure still must execute mcp-typed-confirm.mjs itself and report the result (including the post-approval re-check).

The GET routes are diagnostic-only (prod=false), not a shipped user surface. The 4 mutating POST routes (POST /api/debug/clear-condition, POST /api/debug/logging, POST /api/debug/reset-index, POST /api/debug/trip-condition) are reachable in prod but carry prod session-token auth, unlike the GET diagnostics -- narrowed from a blanket prod=false claim.

The two mandatory lifecycle endpoints in this cohort, GET /api/health and GET /api/status, are NOT opt-in -- they are exercised via `surface:core.health-surface` (sandbox tier) and the collect-evidence.ps1 API sanity ladder, so the blanket opt-in framing applies only to the diagnostics/metrics/telemetry subset.

Remaining members (OPTIONS /*, POST /api/admin/inference/reload, POST /api/admin/runtime/reload, GET /api/meta/openapi.json, GET /api/meta/routes, GET+POST /api/ui/ready) are internal/dev-tooling utility routes with no coherent user surface.

mustWatch.reason: SmartScreen / Defender / Smart App Control / unsigned-publisher warnings on install cannot be reproduced in CI (no clean Windows); every round records the exact prompt text/screenshots and whether automation (/S) was honored.
mustWatch.note: NOT observable under the CURRENT sandbox posture: generate_wsb's LogonCommand force-disables Smart App Control at boot (sandbox-launch.py's generate_wsb, ~line 507-517), and the installer arrives via folder mount, which never attaches Mark-of-the-Web -- so SmartScreen has nothing to trigger on. Making it fire would need BOTH an in-sandbox download (for MOTW) AND skipping the SAC-disable for that round, which trades away the bypass the round needs to function at all. The real fix is code signing (see the comment at sandbox-launch.py ~line 507-517); deferred by owner budget. This is a posture limitation, not a claim the prompts don't exist -- record it as unobservable this round, not as a pass.

mustWatch.reason: Tools installed mid-session (e.g. Node.js by an MSI) are invisible to already-running shells/processes that started before the install -- a stale session PATH reads as 'tool not installed' when it is genuinely on disk. The harness must self-repair (probe well-known install dirs + the MACHINE PATH, not just the session PATH) rather than report a false negative and silently drop coverage; see collect-evidence.ps1's npx/Node PATH-repair gate.
mustWatch.origin: tempdoc 727-followup smoke round: collect-evidence.ps1 falsely reported 'Node.js may not be installed' on its first run, silently dropping all /mcp coverage; not CI-gateable, only reproducible on a genuinely clean environment with staggered installs

mustWatch.reason: An expired/already-consumed authorization pending can still render a fully convincing Authorize dialog -- typing the confirm phrase enables Approve, but clicking Approve (or Deny) silently no-ops with no grant, no error, and no way to dismiss the modal. Invisible to an API-only round (item 4 scored a clean PASS on the API); only the GUI tier surfaced it. Check remains UI-tier until/unless a host RAIL step lands.
